title: XState
description: Model business workflows as state machines with XState v5, run them with actors, and drive React from snapshots.

data.text: XState expresses behaviour as a state machine: a finite set of states, the events that move between them, and the effects each transition runs. Invalid transitions become impossible to reach, which is why checkout and authentication flows benefit most.

data.caption: src/machines/checkoutMachine.ts (XState v5)

data.text: Actions transform context; `invoke` runs async work (here a promise actor) and routes to `onDone` or `onError`. Notice the error path returns to `collecting` with the message in context instead of leaving the machine in a broken state.

data.caption: useMachine plus snapshot checks

data.title: XState v5 changed the API
data.text: `interpret()` was replaced by `createActor()` and `useMachine` from `@xstate/react`. Machines now use promise/logic actors (`fromPromise`, `fromCallback`) instead of services, and `state.matches` reads from a snapshot. Code written for v4 will not compile on v5.

npx @statelyai/inspect   # or paste the machine into stately.ai/viz

rows: Async request with retry and cancel

terms.definition: One of a finite set of modes the machine can be in, such as collecting or validating.
A message (SUBMIT, RETRY) that may trigger a transition.
Extended state that changes during transitions, such as the email value.
A running machine instance; in v5 you create it with createActor and read snapshots.

items.question: When is XState overkill?
items.answer: When the behaviour is a single boolean or a list of independent values. State machines pay off when transitions are constrained by another piece of state and "impossible" combinations keep appearing in bug reports.

items.question: XState or useReducer?
items.answer: useReducer is a state container without a statechart. It cannot describe guards, nested/parallel states, or async invocation, and it will happily accept an event that should be impossible.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Name a concrete flow (checkout, upload, onboarding) where a machine removed impossible states, and be able to explain context versus state and why actors replaced services in v5.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: States are finite; events cause transitions; context stores extended state.
invoke runs async actors and routes success and failure explicitly.
XState v5 uses createActor and snapshot.matches, not interpret.
Use machines for constrained workflows, not for every piece of state.
data.takeaway: XState is the strongest answer when an interviewer asks how you prevent invalid states in a complex flow.
